status: block complete (re-verified after the Open Math OS outage); one exact negative result for a delimited family; residual region open
summary: Decided one exact family for the six-colour side, independent of the cyclic-locus and finite-graph routes: colourings of the plane constant on the cells of a rectangular lattice tiling sZ x tZ (0<s<=t, s^2+t^2<1). Proved the exact criterion: such a colouring is proper iff no colour class contains a difference v with dmin(v)<=1<=dmax(v), the endpoints of the (closed) distance interval of the cell pair; so the family is equivalent to 6-colourability of a Cayley graph of Z^2, and a 7-clique of pairwise-forced offsets refutes 6 colours. Certified in exact integer arithmetic, over a declared 1401-box cover of the whole open region, that every box with s>13/30 plus 16 further anisotropic boxes admit NO proper 6-colouring (681 boxes; all witnesses re-verified in exact rational arithmetic). The remaining 720 boxes have clique number <=6, so this certificate cannot decide them; that region is where a 6-colouring of this family, hence of the plane, would have to live.
verified_results: Lemma (interval): the distance set of two closed lattice rectangles is [dmin,dmax], both ends attained; a same-coloured pair of cells is legal iff 1 is NOT in [dmin,dmax] (tangency = illegal). Proved; boundary cases dmin=1, dmax=1 handled with closed inequalities.

Lemma (equivalence): for 0<s,t, s^2+t^2<1, a proper 6-colouring of the PLANE constant on cells exists iff Cay(Z^2,{v forced}) is 6-colourable. Exact, no measurability needed; edge sets are measure zero and harmless.
Lemma (finite space): forced implies |v| <= 1+sqrt(s^2+t^2), giving explicit windows |p|<=1+60/i0; all tests reduce to integer comparisons with common denominator 60.

CERTIFIED NEGATIVE RESULT: 681 of the 1401 boxes of the grid (i/60,(i+1)/60]x(j/60,(j+1)/60], 1<=i<=j<=59, i^2+j^2<3600, contain a 7-clique among guaranteed-forced differences (monotone box test); hence no proper 6-colouring for ANY (s,t) in them. This includes EVERY box with i>=26, i.e. every s>13/30 with s<=t, s^2+t^2<1, plus 16 anisotropic boxes listed in FINDINGS.md.

Verification: scripts/cells.py selftest (integer test == independent Fraction test on 7 shapes; every guaranteed-box member forced at all 4 corners) -> 'selftest passed: True'; scripts/verify_witness.py re-checks all 681 recorded cliques at 6 sample points each (4086 checks) -> 0 failures.
Sharpness: on the 720 undecided boxes a bounded exact clique search found no 7-clique (maximum 6), so the K_7 certificate provably cannot decide them.

LIMIT LEMMA for the K_7 certificate (proved by me this block, paper-level, not machine-checked): if 7 planar points have all pairwise distances in [a,b] then b >= (sqrt7-1)a [7 disjoint disks of radius a/2 lie in the (a/2)-neighbourhood of the hull: 7 pi a^2/4 <= area(hull) + perim(hull) a/2 + pi a^2/4 with area <= pi b^2/4 (isodiametric) and perim <= pi b (Barbier)]. A forced difference has |v| in [1-D, 1+D], D = cell diameter, so a 7-clique of cells forces D >= 1 - 2/sqrt7 = 0.2441. Consequence: the K_7 method provably cannot decide any tiling with cell diameter below 0.2441; it is a limit on my own method, not a statement about chi(R^2). (The claim surfaced in a refused duplicate proposal of my swarm; I re-derived it rather than trust it.)
conjectures: The rectangular cell family admits no proper 6-colouring for ANY (s,t) in the open region; on the undecided boxes the K_7 obstruction would need a non-clique argument (odd wheel / measure-density argument on the forced Cayley graph).
If a 6-colouring of the plane exists, it is not constant on the cells of a rectangular lattice tiling with min side > 13/30 (now a theorem), and plausibly not on any rectangular tiling.
